metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source code (server.js) with a deployable entry point (app.listen(8080)), a Dockerfile, and Kubernetes deployment manifests present. Classified as application.
metadata.archetype_justification: The primary endpoint (GET /rates) queries MongoDB with filter parameters (origin, dest) and returns results with minimal business logic. POST /quote performs stateless arithmetic computation. No write operations to the database. Read-heavy with minimal transformation.

classification_consistency_check.reason: Score 1.44 yields Not Ready band but 9 High findings (2-11 range) force Remediation Required tier. findings.title: Managed Compute
findings.description: The application is containerized (Dockerfile with multi-stage build targeting Node 18-alpine) and has Kubernetes deployment manifests with 2 replicas, resource limits, and security context. However, no IaC defines the underlying container orchestration platform.
findings.gap: No managed container orchestration service (EKS/ECS/Fargate) is provisioned via IaC. The workload is containerized but the hosting platform is undefined in the repository.
findings.recommendation: Provision an EKS cluster (or ECS/Fargate service) via Terraform or CDK to host the containerized workload.

findings.title: Managed Databases
findings.description: The application connects to a self-managed MongoDB instance at a hardcoded static IP (mongodb://10.0.8.20:27017/shipping). MongoDB 2.4 (EOL October 2016). No authentication, no TLS, no managed database service.
findings.gap: Database is entirely self-managed with no automated failover, patching, scaling, or backup. The database engine is 9+ years past EOL.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Amazon DocumentDB (MongoDB-compatible) or DynamoDB. Provision via IaC with Multi-AZ, automated backups, and encryption at rest.

findings.title: Network Security
findings.description: The Kubernetes service uses ClusterIP and the MongoDB connection targets a private IP (10.0.8.20). Security context is enforced in K8s. However, no NetworkPolicy, no explicit security groups/NACLs in IaC, and no ingress controller with security rules.
findings.gap: Missing NetworkPolicy for pod-level network segmentation. No explicit VPC/subnet/security group configuration in IaC.
findings.recommendation: Add Kubernetes NetworkPolicy to restrict ingress/egress traffic. Define VPC, subnets, and security groups in IaC when provisioning the EKS cluster.

findings.title: API Entry Point
findings.description: No API Gateway, ALB, or CloudFront configured. K8s service is ClusterIP only. A commented-out ALB Ingress example exists but is not active.
findings.gap: No managed entry point providing throttling, auth, request validation, or traffic management.
findings.recommendation: Deploy an ALB Ingress Controller or API Gateway in front of the service. Configure throttling, request validation, and centralized authentication.

findings.title: Auto-Scaling
findings.description: K8s deployment specifies static replicas: 2 with no HPA configured. No auto-scaling for the database.
findings.gap: All capacity is statically provisioned. The workload cannot respond to traffic spikes or scale down during low demand.
findings.recommendation: Add a Kubernetes HPA targeting CPU/memory utilization or custom metrics. Configure auto-scaling on the managed database when migrated.

findings.title: Backup and Recovery
findings.description: No backup configuration for the self-managed MongoDB instance. No aws_backup_plan, no snapshot policies, no point-in-time recovery.
findings.gap: No automated backups for the production data store. Data loss has no recovery path.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to a managed database with automated backups and PITR. If remaining on self-managed MongoDB temporarily, implement automated mongodump with S3 storage.

findings.title: High Availability and Fault Isolation
findings.description: K8s deployment has 2 replicas but no topology spread constraints, pod anti-affinity, or multi-AZ configuration. MongoDB at a single IP indicates single-instance deployment.
findings.gap: No multi-AZ deployment. Database is single-instance. An AZ failure would take down the workload.
findings.recommendation: Configure pod anti-affinity or topology spread constraints. Migrate MongoDB to DocumentDB Multi-AZ or DynamoDB.

findings.title: Infrastructure as Code Coverage
findings.description: No IaC exists. No Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, or Pulumi files. All infrastructure is provisioned manually or managed externally with no in-repo definition.
findings.gap: 0% IaC coverage. Infrastructure is non-reproducible, cannot be disaster-recovered from code, and is subject to configuration drift.
findings.recommendation: Adopt Terraform or CDK to define all infrastructure: EKS cluster, managed database, VPC/subnets/security groups, secrets, and monitoring.

findings.title: CI/CD Automation
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline configuration exists. No GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkinsfile, or CodePipeline. Deployment via SSH + git pull + forever restart.
findings.gap: No automated build, test, or deploy pipeline. No quality gates, no automated testing, no container image build automation.
findings.recommendation: Implement a CI/CD pipeline with stages: lint, test, build Docker image, push to ECR, deploy to EKS. Add automated rollback.

findings.title: Programming Languages
findings.description: Node.js targeting 0.10.x (EOL 2016). Express 3.4.8 (EOL). MongoDB driver 1.4.7 (2014). No AWS SDK. Dockerfile runs on Node 18 with --ignore-engines but code uses deprecated patterns.
findings.gap: Compound legacy: language version (Node 0.10), framework (Express 3), and driver (mongodb 1.4.7) are all severely outdated.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade to Node.js 20+ with Express 4/5, modern MongoDB driver 6.x, async/await patterns, and TypeScript.

findings.title: Monolith vs Microservices
findings.description: Single-file application with all concerns intermixed: authentication, routing, database connections, and business logic. Global shared state. No module separation.
findings.gap: No module boundaries. No separation of concerns. Authentication, routing, data access, and business logic tightly coupled.
findings.recommendation: Refactor into modular structure: separate route handlers, middleware, data access layer (repository pattern), configuration module. Apply Hexagonal Architecture.

findings.title: API Versioning Strategy
findings.description: No API versioning. Endpoints are /rates and /quote with no version prefix, no version headers, no API specification.
findings.gap: No versioning — breaking changes affect all consumers simultaneously with no migration path.
findings.recommendation: Introduce URL-path versioning (e.g., /v1/rates). Create an OpenAPI specification documenting the API contract.

findings.title: Service Discovery
findings.description: MongoDB endpoint hardcoded as static IP in source code. K8s ConfigMap defines MONGO_URL but the application ignores environment variables. No service registry or DNS-based discovery.
findings.gap: All service endpoints hardcoded in application source code. No dynamic service discovery.
findings.recommendation: Refactor to read MONGO_URL from environment variables. Adopt Kubernetes DNS-based discovery or AWS Cloud Map.

findings.title: Unstructured Data Storage
findings.description: Application data stored in self-managed MongoDB. No S3, no managed object storage, no parsing pipeline. Data locked in an unmanaged, EOL MongoDB instance.
findings.gap: No managed object storage. Data inaccessible for modern workloads (analytics, AI, search).
findings.recommendation: Migrate rate data to a managed store (DocumentDB or DynamoDB). Use S3 for any future unstructured data needs.

findings.title: Unified Data Access Layer
findings.description: Database access directly embedded in route handlers. MongoClient.connect() called per request inside GET /rates. No repository pattern, no connection pooling.
findings.gap: No unified data access layer. Database queries directly in route handlers with no abstraction. Per-request connection creation.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a data access module with connection pool and repository pattern exposing typed methods.

findings.title: Database Engine Version and EOL
findings.description: MongoDB 2.4 indicated by source code comment and confirmed by mongodb driver 1.4.7 compatibility. MongoDB 2.4 reached EOL October 2016. No version pinning in IaC.
findings.gap: Database engine 9+ years past EOL. Known security vulnerabilities. No version management strategy.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Amazon DocumentDB (MongoDB 4.0+ compatible) or upgrade to MongoDB 7.x on a managed platform.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest
findings.description: Self-managed MongoDB with no encryption configuration. No KMS keys. No TLS on MongoDB connection (plain TCP to 10.0.8.20:27017).
findings.gap: No encryption at rest configured for the production data store. Data stored in plaintext.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Amazon DocumentDB or DynamoDB (encryption at rest by default). If remaining on self-managed MongoDB, enable WiredTiger encryption.

findings.title: API Authentication
findings.description: Static API key (x-api-key header) for authentication. Key hardcoded as 'ship-2013-abc123-static'. Not token-based, no expiry, no per-consumer keys.
findings.gap: Static API key without token-based auth. No per-consumer keys, no expiry, no rotation.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth2/JWT-based authentication via Amazon Cognito. Use API Gateway authorizers. Remove hardcoded key.

findings.title: Centralized Identity Integration
findings.description: Application manages its own authentication (hardcoded API key comparison). No Cognito, Okta, or external IdP integration. No OIDC/SAML. No SSO.
findings.gap: No centralized identity integration. Standalone hardcoded credential with no federation.
findings.recommendation: Integrate with Amazon Cognito as centralized IdP. Configure OAuth2/OIDC flows.

findings.title: Secrets Management
findings.description: Plaintext credentials hardcoded in source code: API_KEY = 'ship-2013-abc123-static' and MONGO_URL = 'mongodb://10.0.8.20:27017/shipping'. Committed to version control.
findings.gap: Plaintext credentials in source code. API key and MongoDB connection string directly in JavaScript file. No Secrets Manager, no Vault, no rotation.
findings.recommendation: Remove hardcoded secrets. Read from K8s Secrets and ConfigMap (already configured in deployment.yaml). Migrate to AWS Secrets Manager with rotation.

findings.title: Compute Hardening and Patching
findings.description: Dockerfile uses node:18-alpine (minimal) and runs as non-root. K8s enforces security context. However, no automated patching, no vulnerability scanning, no Dependabot/Renovate.
findings.gap: Some hardening (Alpine, non-root) but no automated patching or vulnerability scanning. Dependencies have known CVEs.
findings.recommendation: Add Dependabot or Renovate for automated dependency updates. Enable ECR image scanning. Consider Bottlerocket for production.

findings.title: Application Security Pipeline
findings.description: No security scanning tools. No SAST, no dependency scanning, no container scanning. No CI/CD pipeline to integrate security into.
findings.gap: No security validation. Vulnerabilities in Express 3, mongodb 1.4.7, and NoSQL injection in code go undetected.
findings.recommendation: Add Dependabot/Renovate, Semgrep or SonarQube for SAST, ECR image scanning, and npm audit in build stage.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing
findings.description: No distributed tracing. No OpenTelemetry, X-Ray, or APM. No trace ID propagation.
findings.gap: No ability to trace requests or diagnose production issues. No request correlation.
findings.recommendation: Add OpenTelemetry SDK or AWS X-Ray. Instrument HTTP layer and MongoDB calls. Propagate trace headers.

findings.title: SLO Definitions
findings.description: No SLOs defined. No monitoring artifacts. No CloudWatch alarms. No availability targets.
findings.gap: No formal service level definitions. No mechanism to detect degradation.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs (p99 latency, availability). Implement CloudWatch alarms or SLO monitoring.

findings.title: Business Metrics
findings.description: No custom metrics published. No business outcome tracking. Only default container runtime metrics available.
findings.gap: No business metrics. Cannot measure service value delivery.
findings.recommendation: Instrument business metrics: quotes_generated, rate_lookups, quote_amount. Publish via CloudWatch or OpenTelemetry.

findings.title: Anomaly Detection and Alerting
findings.description: No alerting configured. No CloudWatch alarms. No anomaly detection. Only console.log for startup message.
findings.gap: No alerting. Failures go undetected until user reports.
findings.recommendation: Add CloudWatch alarms for error rate and latency. Enable anomaly detection. Integrate with incident management.

findings.title: Deployment Strategy
findings.description: K8s Deployment uses default RollingUpdate with 2 replicas. Readiness/liveness probes configured. No canary, blue/green, or traffic shifting.
findings.gap: Rolling deployment only. No ability to test new versions with subset of traffic.
findings.recommendation: Implement canary deployments using Argo Rollouts or AWS CodeDeploy with traffic shifting.

findings.title: Integration Testing
findings.description: No tests exist. No test files, no test framework, no npm test script. Zero automated test coverage.
findings.gap: No automated testing. Any change carries full regression risk. Cannot safely refactor or migrate.
findings.recommendation: Add Jest or Mocha. Write integration tests for /rates and /quote. Integrate into CI pipeline.

findings.title: Incident Response Automation
findings.description: No runbooks, no incident response automation, no SSM documents. Only K8s pod restart on probe failure.
findings.gap: No incident response capability beyond pod restart. All handling is ad hoc.
findings.recommendation: Create operational runbooks for common incidents. Implement self-healing automation.

findings.title: Observability Ownership
findings.description: No observability ownership. No CODEOWNERS. No dashboards. No alarms with named owners. No team attribution.
findings.gap: No observability ownership. Monitoring has no clear responsibility assignment.
findings.recommendation: Define observability ownership: service-level dashboards, alarm owners, SLO definitions with team attribution.
